hypothesis: Iter 95 = ONE FRAME ERROR, AND THE FIRST LIVER AXIS. (A0) MassActionModule's consumption term used the normalized DEVIATION from typical where its own docstring says CONCENTRATION. Modules receive normalized state but their rates apply to raw state, so this is the iter-90 Sg frame-error family, and it did two things. It made `typical` an ABSORBING FLOOR for every species: measured on the iter-94 artifact across fast/fed/big-meal/hard-bout, insulin, glucagon, ffa, bhb, lactate and hepatic_output all sit at min-typical = 0.0000 while the teacher takes insulin to 2.81 and hepatic_output to 1.12 — insulin is gate-scored and had never been able to fall below 10 uU/mL. And it MANUFACTURED the iter-51 dead-pathway trap, because sitting at typical required prod=0, i.e. prod_raw -> -inf where the softplus derivative vanishes; on the isolated assembly, asking the deviation frame for an equilibrium at 3.8 returns 10.002 with 1.2e-04 of the gradient surviving, versus 3.800 with 4.4e-01 in the concentration frame. Both frames handle targets ABOVE typical perfectly, which is why meal peaks always worked and fasting troughs never did. The fix adds nothing and deletes SetpointHead (109 lines), whose only purpose was escaping that trap. (A1/A5) Ported the two halves of iter-93's teacher fix that the student never received: the defended glucose level falling as liver glycogen empties (Cahill 2006), and fasting hypoinsulinemia effective_Ib = Ib*min(G/Gb,1)^5 (Polonsky 1988). (A3) NORM_SCALE[bhb] 0.05 -> 0.5: the catastrophe clamp sat at 1.10 mmol/L, BELOW the teacher's own 1.315 at 24 h, and a working bhb would have driven every metabolic head's tanh into saturation at z=+24. LOCAL VALIDATION (18 epochs, 8 patients): all three iter-94 criteria pass — liver_glycogen ratio 1.28, bhb 0.62 (was 0.00), insulin +1.42 (was -0.40, wrong direction). bhb reaches 0.85 @24h / 1.31 @48h vs teacher 1.32, with a PLAIN SpeciesHead: the bespoke ketogenesis and hepatic-output flux forms originally proposed turned out to be unnecessary and were NOT added. Known risk: the fasted chain now OVERSHOOTS (glucose to 54.6 against a 70-85 band, pinned at the fast_gb_floor_frac floor; hr to 54). (B) First hepatobiliary axis: cck, gallbladder_bile, intestinal_bile, bile_acids, simulated in the teacher and structurally modelled in the student. Entered at the MEDIATOR rather than at ALP/GGT/ALT/bilirubin, because those are damage readouts with no driver in this state vector and would ship inert — and the iter-94 ruler finding is that the gate cannot tell a constant from a simulator. Canalicular export is an explicit step so the enzymes can hang off its impairment later. All 7 literature anchors pass in the teacher; the student reproduces CCK peak +15 min, bile-acid peak +88 min and 39% ejection at fresh init, before any training. (C) REVERTED --cold-distill-anchor-local-scale-floor to 0.0. iter-94's benchmark landed 2026-08-21 and iter-94 REGRESSED vs iter-93 on the same ruler (0.0558 -> 0.0825 overall; cgm_real glucose skill -1.099 -> -1.698) despite a baseline handicapped in iter-94's favour. That is consistent with B1's pre-registered risk (teacher agreement up, real-data agreement down) but NOT proven, since most teacher markers regressed too. Either way its original justification — slow markers being inexpressible — is superseded by A0, so it is removed rather than carried as a confound.
